text:
Priya (PM): quick run-through: we need a concise roadmap for long-term routing + multi-region isolation. Sales is getting pressure from two enterprise pilots. can we agree on sequencing today?
Jon (Platform Arch): propose we do platform-first: lightweight policy primitives -> pilot lanes -> hardened ops & billing. primitives should be tiny and composable.
Lina (Eng): agreed. engineering scope idea: implement route descriptors + affinity token + a basic fallback priority list. keep API surface small.
Carlos (SRE): ops asks: include region provenance headers, a tagging schema for cost/chargeback, and a deterministic evacuation path. also need alerting thresholds for cross-region failovers.
Priya (PM): ok, draft acceptance levels so we can tell sales what "pilot" vs "GA" means.
Jon (Platform Arch): rough acceptance (short):
- Pilot: policy primitives live, request tagging in place, one customer routed via fallback chain, documented runbook, smoke chaos test pass.
- GA: multi-customer canary, documented capacity contract, breach playbook exercised, cost telemetry present.
Lina (Eng): will add numeric targets: 99p latency within 2x baseline for pilot; GA should be within 1.2x baseline at 99p.
Carlos (SRE): add reliability checks: pilot needs 2-week observational window with no >5m unplanned evictions. GA requires one month and successful evacuation drill.
Priya (PM): good. now isolation tiers? we previously discussed 3 levels but let's name them slightly different: community, affinity, isolated-dedicated.
Jon (Platform Arch): community = shared pool, no guarantees. affinity = soft isolation: routing affinity + quotas + graceful eviction. isolated-dedicated = dedicated hardware/pool, stronger SLA. map pricing to that.
Lina (Eng): implementation sketch for affinity: attach affinity_token to session, track last_active. eviction algo: LRU with tenancy weight. pseudo snippet: 
```
route(request) {
  if (pool.hasCapacityFor(request.tenant)) return pool.assign(request)
  else return fallbackChain.next(request)
}
onEvict(candidate) {
  if (candidate.tenant == stickyTenant) prefer(olderSessions)
  emit(migration_token)
}
```
Carlos (SRE): telemetry tags we need: tenant_id, isolation_tier, route_variant, model_id, tokens_consumed. also region_origin. these must be in every trace/span.
Priya (PM): sequencing question: build primitives first OR onboard big customers first? Leaning primitives-first so each pilot is smaller. thoughts?
Jon (Platform Arch): primitives-first reduces duplicated work. we can add a feature-flagged policy endpoint to flip per-customer.
Lina (Eng): engineering estimate: primitives + fallback + tagging = 4 sprints for a 3-person squad to have pilot-ready. each pilot integration ~1 sprint with dedicated SE.
Carlos (SRE): add required tests: deterministic fallback simulation (scripted), cross-region latency regress test, cost-regression test. include runbook and automation for rollback.
Priya (PM): draft timeline: spec by next Wed, prototype by end of month, pilot outreach during prototype phase, pilot ramp in 6-8 weeks.
SalesBot: FYI @account-team: customers A and B asked for isolated-dedicated lanes; need contract language.
Jon (Platform Arch): note on ReservedCapacity: affinity & isolated-dedicated will interact with reserved pools. we need migration notices and compatibility layer to prevent customer disruption.
Lina (Eng): will avoid hard schema changes. add compatibility header: X-Rdwood-Routing-Version. default to v1.
Carlos (SRE): operational constraint: any global routing change must go through staged rollout: canary -> regional -> global. automated gating based on error rates & latency.
Priya (PM): action items: 1) Jon write 1-page spec for policy primitives (due Wed), 2) Lina create prototype plan + sketch client header changes (due Fri), 3) Carlos list monitoring+chaos scenarios + SLOs (due Fri). I'll coordinate pilot customers and legal.
Jon (Platform Arch): will include a tiny policy example for early testing (DSL-ish):
```
policy "tenantAffinity" {
  match: tenant in list
  action: prefer(region="us-west-2")
  fallback: prefer(region="us-east-1"), redirect:shared-pool
}
```
Lina (Eng): small note: instrument tokenization points for chargeback. prefer event-based counters at border.
Carlos (SRE): infra note: if we introduce per-tenant eviction tokens we must encrypt them at rest and rotate keys. security review required.
Priya (PM): thanks. let's reconvene Thursday to review Jon's spec. keep messages short in channel so we can capture decisions. :sparkles:
